content:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — GPU pool 'dedicated-prod-us-west-2' exceeding memory and compute thresholds. avg queued requests per shard: 24 (baseline 3). autoscaler attempted 3 scale actions; 2 failed due to per-tenant quota. Marking P1.

sre-oncall: seeing large spike in queueing and token throughput. initial hypothesis: new model rollout (vendor-model-3.1) pushed larger context windows and increased kv-cache pressure.

jordan: confirmed — rollout completed ~09:12 UTC to 40% of traffic per rollout job id `deploy-2026-11`. Metrics: median seq_len increased from 512->1024 for impacted routes. kv cache warmup is causing memory amplification.

priya: is this causing throttles to surface to customers? any 5xx/errors?

henry: yes, rate-limit and token-throttle events spiking. Some requests end up queued past SLO; autoscaler attempted to add GPUs but hit project-level GPU cap (quota) — see error in control-plane: `QuotaExceeded: GPU quota for project x reached`.

incident-bot: Paging @sre-oncall and @platform-oncall. Severity: P1. Impact: 12 customer routes showing >10s tail latency, 3 customers reporting token truncation and elevated errors.

platform-oncall: I can raise emergency quota with cloud provider but that takes ~30-45m. We should attempt immediate mitigations first.

jordan: quick mitigation plan: 1) Pause rollout for vendor-model-3.1 2) Shift affected traffic to fallback model (vendor-model-3.0-quant) 3) Apply temporary per-route max-inflight cap and lower batching window. 4) If safe, force kv-cache eviction policy to LRU-smaller and limit per-shard KV memory.

priya: agree. I'll coordinate rollback/pause and route-shift. @deploy-bot can you stop rollout?

deploy-bot: Received command. Stopping rollout job `deploy-2026-11`. State transition: canary->paused.

henry: routing rule change in progress: rerouting 40% of canary traffic back to vendor-model-3.0-quant via `route-weight` bump. Command run:
```
redwood routes update --route /api/generate --set-weight vendor-model-3.0-quant=40 --user jordan
```

incident-bot: Note: autoscaler still showing queue depth high. Consider reducing per-request kv-cache allocation to speed up eviction.

jordan: changing runtime config: lowering kv_cache.max_entries from 1.2e6 -> 6e5 on affected shards. Patch applied to pool workers with rolling restart.

platform-oncall: rolling restarts started, but restarts will cause transient cold cache and more CPU. Doing in small batches.

customer-success: heads-up — we already have inbound reports from two enterprise customers about truncated responses. I'm drafting customer comms acknowledging degraded latency and a rollback attempt.

sre-oncall: live metrics: queue depth down from 24->10 after route shift and kv limit, token throughput still 2x baseline. Latency tail improving but some shards still at 90% GPU mem.

priya: If quota increase is fast enough we can add 8 GPUs to absorb warmup pressure. Platform, please start quota request and provide ETA.

platform-oncall: Submitted emergency quota request to cloud provider (ticket cp-789234). Cloud response ETA 22m. Meanwhile enabling temporary cross-region overflow to eu-west as fallback.

henry: Applying per-tenant throttle policy for new model variant: max_concurrent_per_tenant=8, to prevent single customers from monopolizing warmup.

jordan: also toggled `batching.max_latency_ms` from 30 -> 10 for affected routes to reduce queue depth. This will increase compute cost but reduces tail latency.

incident-bot: Update: after config changes and route shift, impacted customer routes reduced to 4 with latency >5s. No data exfil or correctness regressions detected.

customer-success: sent proactive note to affected customers at 09:47 UTC. Clarified root cause as model rollout warmup and we paused rollout. Offering prioritized follow-up.

priya: next steps: 1) keep rollout paused 2) monitor kv-cache warming and GPU mem for 2h 3) coordinate with vendor for smaller-context variant or quantized weights 4) if quota granted, plan safe ramp with slower traffic increases and pre-warm caches via synthetic load.

platform-oncall: quota approved by cloud provider at 10:12 UTC, +6 GPUs provisioned. We will not auto-shift traffic until caches warmed.

jordan: re-run smaller canary (5%) with pre-warm: `redwood deploy --model vendor-model-3.1 --prewarm --canary 5` and observe memory footprint.

henry: logging note: capturing heap + kv-cache size snapshots and per-request seq_len histogram for 1h window. Will attach to postmortem.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — P1 -> P2 at 10:35 UTC. All mitigation actions applied; customer impact contained. Please file postmortem with timeline and action items: limit rollout traffic velocity, add pre-warm step for models increasing context, auto-detect seq_len shift and throttle rollout.

priya: filing postmortem now. tagging follow-ups: @platform-oncall (quota playbook), @sre-oncall (auto-throttle rules), @jordan (deploy gating).

customer-success: will follow up with customers and offer credits where appropriate.

sre-oncall: thanks team. Let's keep monitoring for 24h and close once stable.

incident-bot: Thread closed for active coordination. Archive when postmortem uploaded.
